correctness.rationale: No local-field tie for odd parts. Until the first part majority flips, exactly the original majority spins in each part can change, with independent rate-one exponential lifetimes; after first reversal all future changes are monotone to a common sign. The threshold exponentials transform exactly to independent Beta(u+1,a-u) and Beta(v+1,b-v) variables, giving the integer beta sum. Reflection symmetry proves fair fully opposed configurations even with unequal sizes. Survivor-binomial fluctuations and independent quantile CLTs prove the polarization Gaussian window with normalization sqrt[p(2p-1)(1+1/kappa)]. 196 exact rational finite comparisons, 16 fair cases and 3 finite critical-window approximations run from the newly packaged standalone program; only analytical argument proves all n.

value.rationale: The opposed-polarization initial state is a natural two-community metastable conflict for kinetic Ising dynamics. The theorem gives the exact all-size absorbing-phase selection, a nonobvious 1/2 neutrality for unequal fully opposed communities, a sharp Gaussian polarization-difference phase window, and a proved reversal of the *global* initial majority on an infinite sequence of bipartite graphs. These are qualitatively meaningful phase-selection statements, not unmotivated finite slices or known-table entries.
